deities: Sri Sri Radha Govind (Radha-Krishna, presiding deities)

history.period: Established 2008 per a Justdial business listing (verify)
history.summary: The ISKCON temple of Faridabad - known as Sri Sri Radha Govind Mandir - at Geeta Bhawan, C Block, Ashoka Enclave-2, Sector 37, Faridabad 121003. It is the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Gaudiya Vaishnavism) centre for the city, running daily darshan, Bhagavad-gita classes, Sunday programmes with kirtan and prasadam, and spiritual-cultural activities; the temple's own site is iskconfaridabad.com (Facebook: SriSriRadhaGovind). A business listing gives 2008 as the year of establishment (verify); no official founding history was found. Distinct from seq 802 ISKCON Temple, Chandigarh.

name: ISKCON Temple
town_description: Faridabad is Haryana's largest city and a major industrial hub on Delhi's southeastern edge, part of the Delhi NCR. It was founded in 1607 by Shaikh Farid (Mughal emperor Jahangir's treasurer) as Farid's town. Sector 37 and Ashoka Enclave are residential colonies in the newer part of the city toward the Delhi border.

travel.railway: Faridabad Railway Station - about 8-10 km (verify); Sarai Metro Station nearby (verify).
travel.road: Geeta Bhawan, C Block, Ashoka Enclave-2, Sector 37, Faridabad, Haryana 121003; buses and autos serve the sector (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Janmashtami is the grandest celebration; Sunday programmes draw large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30 PM-9:00 PM reported by listing sites (closed 1:00-4:30 PM; verify). Free entry; dress modestly, photography restricted in the sanctum (verify).
